clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock closed the week at 7:35 p.m., essentially unchanged from where it began, a net movement of less than one minute. This near-stillness reflected genuine judicial checks on executive overreach nearly canceling out a dense accumulation of threats, disinformation, and institutional avoidance.

long_synopsis: Week 87 opened with Speaker Mike Johnson declaring Republicans would not accept a Democratic House majority, and closed with Trump banning CNN, MSNBC, and Politico from the White House. Between those bookends, the Supreme Court repeatedly checked the president—on mail ballots, the Federal Reserve, birthright citizenship, and tariffs—while Congress simultaneously handed him sweeping new tariff authority through a Russia sanctions bill. Immigration enforcement deepened its human toll as Temporary Protected Status ended for 350,000 Haitians. DHS was caught inflating non-citizen voter claims by roughly eighty-five times. Racist rhetoric from Republican candidates drew condemnation from some party leaders and defiance from others. The Democracy Clock moved less than a minute, reflecting genuine judicial pushback nearly offsetting a dense pile-up of executive threats and disinformation.
short_synopsis: Judicial rulings against the president nearly canceled out threats to refuse an election outcome, coerced loyalty payments, a press ban, and deepening immigration crackdowns—leaving the clock almost exactly where it started.
